newsitem.title: USA: CME Jan lumber closes limit down, cash trade slow.
newsitem.headline: CME Jan lumber closes limit down, cash trade slow.

text.p: January CME lumber futures closed down the $10.00 per thousand board foot daily limit, pressured by slow cash markets, traders said.
January ended limit down at $399.50 per tbf while the early limit loss in March was pared, with that month closing $7.40 lower at $387.20. Other months ended $7.10 to $3.50 lower.

Futures tumbled after opening higher and quickly running into technical resistance. Selling prompted by slow cash trade then weighed on prices and nearbys fell for limit losses by midday as light sell stops added to weakness. Poor weather should keep cash business quiet, traders said.
"Weather continues to be a negative factor," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Schmaedick also noted that the last rally in cash prices now appears to be mostly short covering from wholesalers. There was not much retail follow-through buying, he said.
Prudential Securities, Smith Barney and Refco sold on the setback, pit sources added.
